correctness.rationale: For each dominating set D, the set of empty clique fibers E is either empty (then |D|>=m) or nonempty. In the latter case, for each h and each z in C=f(E), the cross-edge definition forces a selected vertex with first-coordinate image h and second coordinate z; additionally every occupied fiber needs a selected vertex. The exact optimum at fixed E is sum_h max(t_h,|C|), attained by explicit placement of coordinate representatives while meeting every occupied fiber. For fixed C, taking one occupied layer of each color in C minimizes cost and gives |C|^2+sum_{h notin C}max(a_h,|C|). An exchange argument selects the |C| largest multiplicities. Sorting, the nonsurjective and bijective boundaries, the extrema min(m,n),m, and the n=2 full spectrum all follow exactly. The standalone direct graph checker exhaustively confirms the formula for 82 representative finite profiles. Finite checks are not substituted for the universal proof.

originality.rationale: The motivating papers define the operation and introduce its domination extrema, including a general bound, an upper-extremal theorem, and a degree criterion. The exact value for every individual complete-factor map as a function of its fiber multiplicities, and the unbounded gaps in possible values, are not implied by those statements. Both relevant primary texts were inspected in material detail, and targeted graph-product and domination searches did not reveal a dominating equivalent. Residual publication-priority risk under alternative terminology is explicitly retained.
residual_risks: The accessible queries and inspected texts do not exhaust all mathematical literature or all synonyms for clique-layer products; independent priority assessment may find earlier equivalent statements.
Only the relevant sections and structural coverage of the 23-page original product paper were inspected; no claim that every unrelated appendix was checked.
Computational tests cover 82 finite profiles, not arbitrary graph sizes.

value.rationale: The 2023 Sierpiński domination framework invites exact evaluation of the same invariant as the connecting map varies. The theorem supplies a complete, efficient multiplicity-profile answer for a basic natural two-parameter family, beyond the known general bounds. It also proves the sharp map-surjectivity dichotomy (non-surjective gamma=m versus surjective gamma<=n^2), determines both global extrema, and gives the exact two-color spectrum {2,3,4,m} with unbounded forbidden intervals. The significant mathematical content is the structural compression and attainability gap, not mere independent verification or rebranding a standard bound.
